proof:
# An all-dimensional multi-vertex incidence continuation of a tight joint row

This is a proved family, not a proof of the joint-row inequality for all
simplex circuits. In particular it permits (d) of the (d+1) caps to
capture (d) vertices each. All cuts are proper and the source is interior.

## 1. Definitions and actual simplex

Fix (d\ge2), (0<A<1), and (C<0). Put

\[
t=\frac{1-A}{d},\qquad B=t-(d-1)C,\qquad D=A-dC.
\]

Exclude the single value (C=-t). In \(\mathbb R^d\), use the vertices

\[
P_0=-\frac A d\mathbf1,\qquad
P_j=(t+C)e_j-C\mathbf1\quad(1\le j\le d),
\]

and let (K=\operatorname{conv}(P_0,\ldots,P_d)), (k=|K|).
Its edge determinant is

\[
\det(P_1-P_0,\ldots,P_d-P_0)
 =(t+C)^{d-1}(A+B)\ne0.
\]

The positive barycentric coordinates

\[
\lambda_0=\frac B{A+B},\qquad
\lambda_j=\frac A{d(A+B)}
\]

sum to one and have weighted vertex sum zero. Thus the common source

\(0\in\operatorname{int}K\).

Take the balanced minimal positive normal circuit

\[
v_0=-\mathbf1,\qquad v_j=e_j\quad(1\le j\le d),
\]

and its closed caps (H_i=\{x:v_i\cdot x\ge0\}). The signed vertex
values of row zero are (A,-B,\ldots,-B). For row (j\ge1), they are
\(-A/d\) at (P_0), (t\) at (P_j), and \(-C>0\) at all the
remaining vertices. Hence (H_0) isolates one vertex; every other cap
contains exactly (d) vertices, with none on a cutting plane.

## 2. Exact cap and coarea data

Write (Q_i=|K\cap H_i|/k) and

\[
S_i=\frac{\mathcal H_{d-1}(K\cap\partial H_i)}{k\|v_i\|}.
\]

For a simplex cap with one positive vertex margin (a), its fraction is
\(a^d/\prod(a+b_j)\), where the negative margins are \(-b_j\).
Its normalized coarea measure is (d/a) times its cap fraction. This
follows by using the cut-edge intercepts to compute the homothetic
pyramid determinant; the cap has altitude (a/\|v_i\|), so the
coarea assertion follows from its volume as a pyramid.

Apply that formula to row zero and to the complements of the other
rows. It gives

\[
Q_0=\left(\frac A{A+B}\right)^d,\qquad
S_0=\frac{dA^{d-1}}{(A+B)^d},
\tag{1}
\]

and, for every (j\ge1),

\[
Q_j=Q:=1-\frac{A^d}{D^{d-1}},\qquad
S_j=S:=\frac{d^2A^{d-1}}{D^{d-1}}.
\tag{2}
\]

Here (0<Q<1), since (D>A\) and (A<1). These identities use the
actual coarea measures for the specified, balanced normal lengths.
In particular no independent row rescaling is made.

Let

\[
M=\sum_{i=0}^d\frac{Q_i}{S_i}
  =\frac{D^{d-1}}{dA^{d-1}},\qquad
f_i=\frac{dQ_i^{(d-1)/d}}{S_iM}.
\tag{3}
\]

These are precisely the raw-volume quantities in the question:

\[
f_i=\frac{d k^{1/d}|K\cap H_i|^{(d-1)/d}}
 {\sigma_i\sum_j |K\cap H_j|/\sigma_j},
\qquad \sigma_i=kS_i.
\]

Equations (1)–(3) simplify to

\[
f_0=\frac{dA^{d-1}(A+B)}{D^{d-1}},\qquad
f_1=\cdots=f_d=Q^{(d-1)/d}=:x\in(0,1).
\tag{4}
\]

## 3. The selected joint row is strictly below its bound

Put (p=d/(d-1)). The selected row has the exact value

\[
\begin{aligned}
\Phi_0
 &=f_0+(d-1)\left(\frac{f_1+\cdots+f_d}{d}\right)^p\\
 &=d-1+\frac{A^{d-1}[1-d(d-1)C]}{(A-dC)^{d-1}}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{5}
\]

Set (u=-dC/A>0). The last fraction equals

\[
\frac{1+(d-1)Au}{(1+u)^{d-1}}<1,
\]

because ((1+u)^{d-1}\ge1+(d-1)u>1+(d-1)Au).
Thus (\Phi_0<d) for every member of the family. As (C\uparrow0),
the other caps pass through (d-1) vertices each and the selected row
converges to equality. This proves stability in this particular
incidence-changing direction; it does not assert stability in all
directions or a neighborhood theorem.

## 4. All the other rows also satisfy the inequality

We use the following elementary two-level-vector fact. If (0\le x\le1)
and (0\le z\le d-(d-1)x^p), then

\[
x+(d-1)\left(\frac{z+(d-1)x}{d}\right)^p\le d.
\tag{6}
\]

The left side increases with (z). At its allowed maximum, set

\[
U(x)=1+\frac{d-1}{d}(x-x^p),\qquad
F(x)=x+(d-1)U(x)^p.
\]

Writing (r=x^{1/(d-1)}), direct differentiation gives

\[
F'(x)=1-U(x)^{1/(d-1)}[dr-(d-1)].
\]

This is nonnegative when (dr\le d-1). Otherwise put (w=1-r\in[0,1/d)).
Then (U\le1+[(d-1)/d]w), and

\[
U(1-dw)^{d-1}
 \le(1+[(d-1)/d]w)(1-dw)\le1.
\]

Thus (F'\ge0) everywhere, with the endpoint derivative interpreted by
continuity. Since (F(1)=d), (6) follows. For (x<1) it is strict:
the derivative is strictly positive below one by the same estimates.

In (4)–(5), (z=f_0<d-(d-1)x^p). Applying (6) gives every remaining
row (\Phi_j<d). This completes the proof for the actual family.

## Scope

The result includes arbitrary (d\ge2), genuine minimal circuits,
interior sources, and caps with several vertices. It neither proves
nor disproves the joint-row assertion for arbitrary simplex circuits.
It also imposes no common-section-centroid assumption. There is no
mixed-integer depth conclusion.
